messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: High 5xx error rate observed for /v1/infer (us-west-2a). AlertID: A-9876. Initial spike at 2024-11-12T09:00:00Z. Symptoms: sustained TCP retransmits from instances in subnet 10.0.32.0/24; NLB target health flapping. See metrics: https://metrics.redwood.ai/alerts/A-9876 :rotating_light:
ben-oncall: taking. pinging infra + net. assigning page. any active maintenance in us-west-2a?
carla-eng-net: not that I'm aware of. I see a sudden TX error burst on a subset of g5-inference hosts (hostnames: inf-g5-az1a-0{12..15}). Kernel tx-queues showing drops, ifconfig shows tx errors incrementing.
alice-ops: KV cache miss rate jumped ~3x across those hosts, model p95 latency doubled. Autoscaler hasn't replaced evicted pods yet — we're seeing node-level network timeouts.
ben-oncall: ok, let's limit blast radius. shunt traffic away from az1a. changing routing policy to prefer us-west-2b with 60s ramp. @sre-rotations please execute steer.
sre-rotations: executing routing shift now. command: `redwood route update --policy region-preference --fallback us-west-2b --weight us-west-2a=10 --weight us-west-2b=90`
carla-eng-net: confirmed NLB is deregistering targets from the problematic host set. however controlplane health checks still show intermittent connect errors for a few ephemeral instances — looks like upstream subnet gateway retransmits. digging with vpc flow logs now.
david-se: can we enable model fallback (smaller quantized variant) for customer-facing routes to reduce GPU mem pressure while we drain nodes? This will reduce token cost and lower allocation pressure.
alice-ops: already staging fallback on canary. Patch to routing: `routes: {model: "redwood/gpt-small-q4", canary: 5%}`. rolling to 100% for affected customers if metrics look stable.
evelyn-cust-sr: heads-up: customer-impact assessment in progress. CS dashboard shows ~1.2% of active customers saw elevated latencies and a handful reported request failures in the last 12m. prepping comms for top 10 accounts.
carla-eng-net: vpc flow logs show a burst of ICMP fragmentation and repeated TCP retransmits originating from the AZ's primary NAT gateway IP. Vendor noted partial degradation on that AZ earlier. Raising contact with cloud-NOC now.
ben-oncall: plan: 1) keep routing shift to us-west-2b (reduce az1a to minimal), 2) drain and replace affected nodes in az1a, 3) enable model fallback for user-facing endpoints, 4) notify customers and update status page. anyone see a risk with changing weights further?
david-se: risk: slight increase in cross-AZ latency for long-running streams but within SLO for most tenants. recommend enabling streaming-prefetch to mask additional RTT where possible.
sre-rotations: started `kubectl drain inf-g5-az1a-012` on three nodes, auto-recreate group scaling triggers next. logs: ```drain: evicting pods (grace 30s)
error: some pods refused eviction (kvcache-writer) -> restarting deployment with lower replicas```
alice-ops: workaround: bump kvcache replica to 2 in az1b before evict so replication completes. Applying now.
evelyn-cust-sr: drafting short note: "We're seeing a regional network issue in us-west-2a causing transient inference failures; traffic is being routed to healthy zones and mitigations are underway. We'll update within 30 minutes." Approving with @ben-oncall.
carla-eng-net: cloud-NOC responded: they're seeing degraded connectivity on physical fabric feeding the AZ's public subnet. They've opened a ticket and are diverting transit. Estimated mitigation window 20-40m.
ben-oncall: thanks. continue draining and monitoring. I'll post interim status on status.redwood.ai: `us-west-2a network degradation impacting inference endpoints; traffic shifted; mitigation in progress.`
david-se: after nodes reconstructed, we'll run a canary against az1a with small load and confirm KV cache warmup, then slowly re-weight.
sre-rotations: canary run scheduled in 25 minutes. current p95 across control plane is down to pre-incident levels in us-west-2b.
evelyn-cust-sr: sent initial comms to top affected customers, leaving note in Zendesk for any inbound.
ben-oncall: thumbs. if cloud-NOC gives full repair earlier we can re-balance quicker. keep alerts muted for known targets to avoid alert fatigue, but keep this thread updated. :thumbsup: 
incident-bot: Incident A-9876 updated: status -> mitigation; assignees -> ben-oncall, carla-eng-net, alice-ops.
ben-oncall: handing to night oncall in 40m. @sre-rotations please prepare handoff doc with: actions taken, current routing weights, nodes replaced, canary results, customer comms links.
sre-rotations: will add handoff notes and ping the rotation owner.
carla-eng-net: last note: watch for asymmetric path after reweight — packet capture shows occasional MSS clamping on older nat gateway. If we see reappearance of retransmits post-rebalance, escalate to cloud-NOC with packet captures.
ben-oncall: copying that into runbook. closing active paging. will reconvene if new alerts.
